From: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Acme: order form redlines + breach carve-out question

Hannah / team — reviewed the redlines and Acme's suggested changes. High level: we should avoid an unanchored reduction to the overall liability cap but we can accept a narrowly scoped sub-limit for breach-specific direct remediation costs with careful carve-outs and trigger mechanics. Key points below (suggested language to follow):

1) Scope of sub-limit: limited to (a) reasonable third-party forensic costs, (b) customer notification and crediting costs, and (c) actual documented regulatory fines that are directly caused by our breach (if any). Exclude consequential, speculative, or lost-margin claims.

2) Quantum: propose a sub-limit equal to the lesser of $1.5M or 25% of the aggregate liability cap for security incidents — this keeps our aggregate exposure predictable while giving the customer targeted comfort.

3) Trigger and coordination with Security Addendum: trigger only after we have confirmed an incident via incident response (internal SOC + third-party forensics where applicable). Any SLA credits in the Security Addendum should be provided in addition to remediation payments, not deducted from the sub-limit (we need to avoid double-counting).

4) Allocation waterfall: remediation expenses (forensics, notification) are payable first against the sub-limit; broader third-party claims/indemnities remain subject to the overall cap and indemnity buckets.

5) Transparency and audit: allow customer to request copies of forensic reports subject to redaction for our confidential tooling; allow a neutral third party if disputes arise.

6) Insurance & mitigation: represent that we maintain commercially reasonable cyber insurance; encourage retention of insurers' subrogation rights.

I'll draft contract text for insertion into the MSA + a short Order Form clause. If you want, I can propose two versions: one customer-friendly and one legal-preferred.

Neha
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.i@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.s@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Acme: order form redlines + breach carve-out question

Great guidance, Neha — thanks. Commercially, Acme is sensitive to anything that looks like "we won't pay for breaches." We can offer the following to bridge:
- ERT (emergency response team) on-call for 90 days post-incident at no charge (worth ~16 hrs/week).
- One-time implementation credit equal to 50% of the first month of committed spend if they accept our proposed sub-limit language.
- Faster incident playbook and monthly sync with their security team for the first quarter after go-live.

If Legal can land on the 25% / $1.5M structure we'll use credits/ERT to sweeten rather than raise the sub-limit.

Karthik
Director, Sales

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.s@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Klein <jordan.k@acme-analytics.com>, Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.i@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Acme: order form redlines + breach carve-out question

Jordan / Rachel — thanks for sending over the spreadsheet. We wanted to share an interim approach that balances Acme's request and Redwood's need for a predictable aggregate cap. High level proposal below; Neha's legal team and I will follow up with exact contract text.

Proposal (summary):
- Sub-limit for "Security Incident Remediation" defined narrowly (forensics, legally required notification, regulator fines directly caused by the incident).
- Sub-limit quantum: the lesser of $1.5M or 25% of the aggregate liability cap in the Order Form.
- SLA credits under the Security Addendum do not reduce this sub-limit; they are separate remedies.
- We will include an allocation waterfall and audit rights for forensic reports (reasonable redactions).
- Additional commercial sweeteners: 90-day ERT at no charge and a one-time implementation credit if Acme accepts the contract language.

Attached is a short one-paragraph change to the Order Form and a marked-up Security Addendum table for clarity. Please let us know if Acme can live with the carve-out scope + quantum or if you'd prefer a higher dollar cap in exchange for reduced credits.

Thanks — Hannah
From: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@acme-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.s@redwood.ai>, Jordan Klein <jordan.k@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.i@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Acme: order form redlines + breach carve-out question

Hannah — appreciate the transparent approach. A couple of quick clarifications from Acme GC: 
1) We need the sub-limit to explicitly include reasonable credit-monitoring costs where Acme is required by law to offer them after a breach.
2) The trigger should not be unilateral — Acme wants an agreed incident classification (e.g., confirmed data exfiltration of customer PII) or an independent third-party determination.
3) Can the parties commit to an expedited external dispute resolution (binding arbitration) only for matters where the amount in dispute relates to whether the sub-limit applies (not for liability quantum)?

If Redwood agrees to the above points, Acme can accept the 25% structure; otherwise they will ask for a fixed $2.5M sub-limit. We are OK with the ERT as a commercial concession but prefer credits not to be the sole remedy.

— Rachel Lim
General Counsel, Acme Analytics
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.s@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@acme-analytics.com>, Jordan Klein <jordan.k@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.i@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2026 18:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Acme: order form redlines + breach carve-out question — agreement path

Rachel / Jordan — thanks, that's helpful. Neha and I spoke and here's the final path we propose: 

1) Include credit-monitoring explicitly as part of "Notification & Remediation" costs (subject to reasonableness standard and documentation).
2) Incident classification: we accept a two-step trigger — (i) Redwood confirms an incident via its SOC and, if disputed, (ii) an independent third-party forensic report (mutually agreed vendor) that establishes the scope. The cost for the independent report will be borne by the party that loses the dispute.
3) Expedited arbitration: we will accept an expedited binding arbitration clause limited to disputes over whether the sub-limit applies (not quantum).

Neha will drop formal MSA redline text into the doc tomorrow morning. If Acme accepts these three items, Karthik and I can move to signature with the $1.5M / 25% structure and the commercial concessions.

Final ask of Acme: confirm acceptance by EOD Fri so we can preserve the proposed pricing in the Order Form.

Appreciate the quick collaboration.

— Hannah
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
